title: The Sigil of the Sundered Sea
premise: In the port city of Vhalen, magic is a crime and Felix Marchetti — last of the oath-bound swordspeakers — has survived three years by selling harmless charms and speaking to no one of what they are. When the crown's witch-hunters seize their found family of smugglers and charm-sellers, Felix learns the youngest, Nia, has been sold as a soul-bond to the court beneath the mountain, where the drowned king harvests gifted souls to hold back the Sundered Sea itself. Felix must gather a crew of the outlawed and the desperate, break into the mountain, and choose between freeing Nia and shattering the seal that keeps the sea from drowning the coast. In the end Felix speaks the forbidden oath, taking Nia's place as the seal's living anchor — until the found family, refusing the price, breaks the bargain entirely and remakes the seal from shared, willing oaths, ending both the hunt and the drowned king's reign.
about_author: Vesper Pemberton is a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing shipwreck ledgers before turning to fiction, and it shows in every tide-worn detail of their prose. They live in a coastal town where the fog comes in on schedule, and they write at a desk salvaged from a decommissioned lightship.

chapters.title: Charms for the Godless
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. In Vhalen's night market, Felix sells a luck-knot to a dockworker and pockets the coin with practiced guilt, hiding the true power coiled in their voice. A child, Nia, watches too closely. The beat is weary concealment — the loneliness of a gift worn as a disguise.

chapters.title: The Proclamation
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Criers announce the crown's Purification Edict: all gifted souls to be registered or taken. Felix burns their charm stock and warns the smuggler household — Brannick, Odile, and Nia — but Odile refuses to run from the city that raised her. Fear arrives as bureaucracy; the beat is the first crack in safety.

chapters.title: Salt and Iron
chapters.summary: Brannick's POV. Witch-hunters in salt-iron masks raid the harbor district. Brannick holds the alley door so Odile and Nia can flee, and is taken. Felix watches from a rooftop, oath-bound never to draw their sword for show — and breaks the rule for the first time, cutting down one hunter. The beat is the point of no return.

chapters.title: What Nia Knew
chapters.summary: Nia's POV. Nia reveals she has been dreaming of the court beneath the mountain — a drowned king who already knows her name, because a broker sold her bond before the edict was even signed. The hunt isn't random; it's harvest. The beat is betrayal: the law was never the real predator.

chapters.title: The Broker's Ledger
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Felix and Odile squeeze a soul-broker in the Tanneries, learning Nia's bond is registered to the court and must be reclaimed before the next tide-moon, when the seal is renewed. They have nineteen days. The beat is cold resolve replacing panic.

chapters.title: A Crew of the Outlawed
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile recruits: Sefa, a tide-reader; the twins Ivo and Rell, lock-wrights; and Maren, a disgraced hunter who knows the mountain's protocols. Each joins for their own unpaid debt. The beat is found family assembling from wreckage, wary and transactional.

chapters.title: The Road Under the Cliffs
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The crew travels the drowned coast road, where Felix teaches Nia small wards and admits, for the first time, what a swordspeaker's oath actually cost — their name, spoken into a blade. Nia starts calling them by a new one. The beat is tenderness hardening into commitment.

chapters.title: Maren's Confession
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Maren reveals she once delivered a gifted soul to the court and heard it singing in the crate for three days. She knows the mountain's gate-rites because she performed them. The crew nearly turns her out; Felix vouches. The beat is guilt offered as service.

chapters.title: The Gate of Nine Questions
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. At the mountain's sea-gate, the crew must answer the gate-rites truthfully while Sefa masks their gifts. Rell's lie costs them — an alarm tolls — and they enter as the mountain wakes. The beat is dread sharpened by wonder at the drowned court's beauty.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Inside, the court is lit by bottled souls, and the drowned king — courteous, ancient, drowning — receives them as guests. He offers Felix a place: a swordspeaker's oath could strengthen the seal and spare Nia. The beat is temptation dressed as mercy.

chapters.title: Nia, Found
chapters.summary: Nia's POV. Nia, held in the soul-nursery, has been treated gently — and has begun to hear the sea through the seal, to love it. She isn't sure she wants to leave. The beat is the horror of a cage made comfortable.

chapters.title: Nineteen Becomes Nine
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. A failed bribery of the court's steward costs the crew three days and Ivo's freedom — he's bonded as collateral. The tide-moon deadline halves. Odile, who never wanted this war, takes command. The beat is leadership forged under loss.

chapters.title: The Soul-Nursery
chapters.summary: Felix and Maren's POV, alternating. They infiltrate the nursery and reach Nia, but Nia resists: leaving means the seal weakens and the coast floods. Felix cannot promise the sea will be held any other way. The beat is the price of survival made literal and small-voiced.

chapters.title: What the Seal Is
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Sefa reads the seal's architecture and discovers the truth: the drowned king was once its anchor, a swordspeaker like Felix, consumed over centuries. The seal doesn't need a soul — it needs an oath freely renewed. The king forgot. The beat is revelation as liberation.

chapters.title: Ivo's Bargain
chapters.summary: Rell's POV. Rell trades herself to the steward to free Ivo, and the twins swap places with a kiss on the forehead and no goodbye. The crew is fracturing into sacrifices. The beat is love expressed as terrible arithmetic.

chapters.title: The King's Drowning
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Felix confronts the drowned king, who confesses he took bonded souls because his own oath ran dry and he was afraid. Felix offers him the thing no one offered in three hundred years: release. The king refuses — fear is all he has left. The beat is pity for the monster.

chapters.title: The Tide-Moon
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. The renewal rite begins; hunters arrive at the mountain's gates, having tracked the crew, and Odile holds the entrance with Maren's stolen protocols while Felix fights toward the seal-chamber. The beat is chaos, loyalty under fire, and Odile finally drawing blood for her people.

chapters.title: The Oath Spoken
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. In the seal-chamber, Felix speaks the forbidden oath to take the king's place — and Nia stops them, speaking her own oath instead: not as a bonded soul but freely given, the first willing anchor in centuries. The seal flares and accepts her. The beat is triumph inverted — the child volunteers, and it breaks Felix's heart.

chapters.title: Breaking the Bargain
chapters.summary: Nia's POV. Inside the seal, Nia finds the king's original oath still intact beneath his fear, and calls the whole crew — bonded, bleeding, arriving — to add their voices. A seal woven from many willing oaths needs no single sacrifice. The king dissolves, grateful at last. The beat is found family as literal architecture of salvation.

chapters.title: The Sea Recedes
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The Sundered Sea settles; the mountain's court crumbles into honest ruin; the hunters outside find only rubble and no souls to claim. Rell is freed in the collapse. Felix's sword — holding their old name — cracks and releases it. The beat is exhaustion, grief, and the return of a name.

chapters.title: Edict Undone
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. In Vhalen, the crew presents the court's ledgers to the crown: the hunt was harvest, the edict a procurement contract. The edict collapses in scandal; the gifted are quietly pardoned. Odile declines a medal and reopens the smuggler house as something new. The beat is justice outside the law, won and then made unnecessary.

chapters.title: A Name Worth Keeping
chapters.summary: Felix's POV, with Nia's coda. On the harbor wall, Felix teaches the first class of new swordspeakers — Nia among them — that an oath freely given costs nothing and gives everything. The luck-knots in the market now sell themselves. The beat is homecoming: the price of survival was never meant to be paid alone.
